A function can have more than one zero or no zeros at all. Graphically, the zeros of a function are the coordinates of the intercepts. Consider the following function as an example. Since this is the only solution to the equation, it is also the only zero of the function. If a function does not intercept the axis, there will be no real solution for the resulting equation when the function rule is set equal to In such a case, the function will have no zeros.
